summary: v08 as a single decision with a stated probability, for pool models without log-probabilities: the judgement session only (no verification); the case score is the submitted p_ischemic.

Aspect B (tools and evidence): v08p plus the annotator-like ST reference (annotator_reference, Smrdel & Jager three-step reference re-applying the LTSTDB episode rule at 100 and 150 uV) in the dossier, with a tool description that says how to read it in both directions.

Aspect A (knowledge): p01 with the heart-rate reference knowledge rewritten from verified cards (K01, K02, K04, K14, K36 for; K10, K32, K33 against; K42, K43 on recurrence), so that a heart-rate rise, heart rate peaking before the ST extremum and recurring episodes are no longer read as evidence against ischemia, while tachycardia-only depression, slow-rate early repolarization and supraventricular tachyarrhythmia count against.

Aspect C (reasoning procedure): p02 with a two-question judgement procedure (Q1 genuine transient episode or drift/level/position/noise, read first from annotator_reference; Q2 ischemic or heart-rate related, counted from three items each way) in which every measurement answers only one question, rule-outs are not filed against ischemia, and p_ischemic is read from a 3x3 table of the two answers.

Aspect A (knowledge): p02 with ST-shape reference knowledge from verified cards (K25, K26 and the database's ischemic description for horizontal or downsloping depression; K25, K37 and the database's heart-rate description against rapid upsloping J-point depression and T-wave changes; K24 against K25 on slow upsloping depression; K21 on the heart-rate-dependent ST point), so that a deep, slowly upsloping depression or a positive ST slope alone is no longer filed against ischemia.

Aspect A (knowledge): p02 with QRS-change reference knowledge from verified cards (K18, K19, K16 for ischemia; K13, K14, K15, K27 for position or artifact), so that a QRS change that grows and recedes gradually with a large ST change in the same lead is no longer read as an axis or position shift by itself, while step-like onset or offset, motion artifact, little heart-rate change, PQ moving with ST, or a QRS change outside the ST lead or outlasting the ST change still count for position.

Aspect B (tools and evidence): p02 plus the heart-rate rise ledger (hr_rise_ledger: ST persisting after heart rate is back at baseline, size, duration and load of the preceding heart-rate rise, and the ST change of the patient's comparable heart-rate rises) in the dossier, with a tool description that reads each measurement in both directions from verified cards (K01, K02, K04, K05 for; K10, K14, K36 against; K03, K07, K08, K42, K43 as cautions).

Aspect C (reasoning procedure): p02 with a final judgement step that bounds p_ischemic by the annotator_reference row (episode at 150 uV in any involved lead: 0.45-0.95; at 100 uV only: 0.25-0.80; absorbed at 100 uV in every involved lead: 0.05-0.60; K22) and places it inside that range by the model's own balance of the other evidence, keeping holistic judgement instead of a fixed table.

Aspect C (reasoning procedure): p02 with the annotator_reference row read at the start of the judgement and used as the range of p_ischemic (episode at 150 uV in any involved lead: 0.45-0.95; at 100 uV only: 0.25-0.80; absorbed at 100 uV in every involved lead: 0.05-0.60; K22), with p placed inside the range first by the model's balance of the other evidence and then, in both directions, by how far the change stands out from that reference (larger: up, K26; smaller: down, K17), so that values spread instead of piling up at the bottom of a range.

Aspect B (tools and evidence): p02 with annotator_reference in the dossier replaced by st_reference_check (same Smrdel & Jager reference and numbers, plus how a change was absorbed: step absorption split by whether a QRS-shape step lies within 144 s of the candidate, the steps behind it, and whether the change goes against the lead's orientation), with a description that reads orientation absorption as clearly against, step absorption with a QRS-shape step as against (K14), and step absorption from the change's own ST-level step as neither direction.
